confidence_note: The old text's turning point ('that night he said I choose to survive and dropped the victim story') could not be tied to the book and is dropped, as is the old text's 'racism at school' as a childhood fact (the sources place racism in Indiana later). Kept: Trunnis Goggins's roller rink where the family worked nights, the belt, the escape to Brazil, Indiana when David was 8 with his mother, using a credit card she got by persuading his father and a neighbour's help, the brother staying, public housing at $7 a month and a $123 welfare check, stutter and hair loss in third grade, being labelled stupid and cheating to stay enrolled. These agree across Deploy Yourself, LifeClub and Shortform summaries; the book itself was not read. The night, the car and the hour of the escape are not described in the sources and are left out.
facts: David Goggins was born in 1975 and grew up in New York with his mother, father and older brother.
His father, Trunnis, owned a roller rink and the family worked there most nights until midnight.
Between ages 6 and 8 David's job was looking after the skating shoes.
The family slept in the rink's office; Trunnis beat his wife with a belt when she disobeyed and beat David with the belt if he tried to protect her.
When David was 8, his mother talked Trunnis into letting her get a credit card in her name.
With a neighbour's help she planned an escape and drove with David to Brazil, Indiana. His older brother stayed with their father.
In Indiana they lived in public housing, paying $7 a month in rent, on a part-time wage and a $123 monthly welfare check.
In third grade David developed a stutter, lost hair and had patches of skin lose colour, which the book ties to toxic stress.
Teachers called him stupid, and he cheated on homework and tests to stay in school, so he could barely read by his teens.
After her ear-infection hospital visit with David, Trunnis beat his wife again.
David was the only Black child in his class and was threatened with expulsion or special-needs placement.
scene_details: a roller rink open until midnight
a credit card in the mother's name
tension: A boy who looked after skates until midnight left in a car with his mother, and the escape did not end the trouble.
opening_idea: Start with the job a six-year-old had at his father's roller rink.

lessons.idea: What happened to you is not your fault, and you can still choose what to do with it next.
lessons.anchor: The escape at eight, then the cheating and the stutter in Indiana.

reflect_final: Which thing that happened to you is not your fault, but still shapes how you act, and what is one move that is yours to make?

use_cases.situation: A friend blames their past for a setback.
use_cases.move: Say the past is real, then ask what the next small thing is that only they can do.
Write down what was out of your hands and what was yours, and act on the second.

use_cases.situation: A child is struggling at school.
use_cases.move: Tell them the label is not the whole picture and ask what they want to try next.

pocket_idea: Goggins's mother left with a credit card and a neighbour's help: you may not choose what happened, but you choose the next move.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: At six David Goggins looked after skates at his father's rink until midnight, and at eight he left with his mother in a car.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: David Goggins grew up working nights at his father's roller rink, with a belt waiting at home for anyone who stepped out of line. When he was 8, his mother talked his father into a credit card in her name, a neighbour helped, and they drove to Brazil, Indiana. His brother stayed. Life there was poor and hard in new ways: a stutter, hair loss, teachers who called him stupid.
